memo:
EdgeHound Performance Review — 14 June 2026

The fund is down 12.47% on 23 settled trades, with realized losses of -$1,354. The dominant driver is MOMENTUM, which has produced -$1,027 on 20 trades (7 wins, 35% win rate). Critically, the Brier score of 0.285 indicates poor probability calibration — the model is systematically overconfident, entering positions where pPredicted clusters tightly around 0.62 regardless of true edge. This mechanical pPredicted uniformity is a red flag: the signal appears to be stamping a fixed confidence rather than discriminating market-specific edge.

A structural pattern in the losses is notable: MOMENTUM has repeatedly taken YES positions on geopolitical/low-probability markets (Iran peace deal, Strait of Hormuz, US invasion) at entries of 0.16–0.26, with pPredicted of 0.54–0.62. These are low-probability, high-uncertainty events where momentum signals are particularly unreliable — price spikes here often reflect noise, not informed flow. The two large sports losses (Udvardy -$522, Vitality CS2 -$255, Trungelliti -$219) suggest MOMENTUM is also misfiring on live-event markets where prices move on outcomes the model cannot access.

SMART_CONSENSUS placed one trade at $1,000 stake — far too large for an unvalidated signal — and lost -$385 immediately. SHORT_FAVORITE is the only profitable engine (+$58, 1W/1L/1 flat).

Current config already has MOMENTUM, SMART_CONSENSUS disabled. I will maintain this and keep parameters conservative: pMin elevated, kellyMult at floor, maxEventExposure capped. VOLUME_SPIKE and ELITE_FOLLOW remain enabled with zero trades — they need data before judgment.
